title: Market correlation matrix for model outage impact on feature adoption
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: create an evidence-backed correlation matrix that quantifies how model provider outages or degradations propagate into measurable drops in feature adoption, revenue, and customer satisfaction across representative customer archetypes. Deliverables: 1) cleaned dataset linking outage windows to feature-level usage (CSV); 2) correlation matrix + interactive heatmap covering top 10 externally-hosted models and top 8 high-value Redwood features (embeddings, chat, RAG, reranking, streaming); 3) a decision spreadsheet for Sales/CS to compute customer-specific outage exposure and recommended fallback policy (quantization/budgeted model substitution); 4) short playbook for product and runtime on rollout thresholds and SLA-based mitigation actions. Method: combine telemetry (token success/error rates, latency percentiles), billing/usage signals, historical provider incident timelines, and 12 customer interviews (targeting PLG startups, mid-market product teams, and a regulated enterprise). Use statistical controls for seasonality and confounding product launches. Tie outputs to unit economics (revenue-at-risk per hour of outage) so PM/GTMs can prioritize fallback investments. This ticket coordinates PM scoping, a small Eng instrumentation spike, and 1 analyst to build the matrix and artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Correlation matrix contains at least 10 model variants and 8 feature buckets with clear interpretation for each cell

Decision spreadsheet accepts customer-specific inputs (monthly token volume, percent critical feature usage, SLA tolerance) and outputs a recommended fallback configuration and estimated hourly revenue-at-risk
Field probe dataset includes anonymized telemetry from at least 15 production outage windows across 8 customers
Runtime engineering has validated the signal ingestion pipeline and a prototype can compute exposure for a sample customer in under 5 minutes
Playbook includes clear SLO thresholds and two recommended automated fallback flows (graceful degrade + model substitution) and is reviewed by Security and Observability leads

decisions: Anonymize customer IDs and bucket by three archetypes (PLG startup, mid-market, regulated-enterprise) to preserve signal while avoiding PII exposure
Use 30-minute rolling windows as the primary outage unit for correlation; supplement with 5-minute and 4-hour windows for sensitivity analysis
Prioritize model variants that constitute >5% of global token volume in the last 90 days to keep matrix tractable
Expose a simple binary exposure flag and a continuous revenue-at-risk estimate in the decision tool to balance clarity and precision
